runners_data.name: Lavender Bloom
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up filly for Steph Hollinshead and David Egan, finishing sixth twice at Goodwood recently but her best run came over 5f at Southwell; 18 days fresh and goes on firm, but needs the pace to be hot enough to reel in an uncontested leader.|

runners_data.name: Geemann
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's gelding has a consistent habit of fading in the finish — a concern flagged in the data — and his last five runs show he rarely threatens at the business end on good or softer ground; though his natural style is hold-up, the small field means he will likely find himself in midfield rather than his preferred deep position, tempering his prospects further.|

runners_data.name: Reality Queen
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's filly has been mixing hold-up runs with midfield efforts and her recent form over 5-6f at Goodwood and Sandown shows she can hit the frame (4th, 5th) without winning; Alistair Rawlinson takes the ride and she is 11 days fresh, with her ability to track Rosieisme Darling from close range making her the most interesting hold-up-adjacent runner in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Rosieisme Darling
runners_data.note: Luke Morris's mount is the only confirmed front-runner and will stride to the lead unchallenged from flag fall; she has placed consistently in a similar vein (3rd, 2nd, 4th recently) suggesting she does not always win from the front, but the firm ground, flat track, and absence of any pace rival gives her the clearest tactical advantage in this race, though the STYLE_FIT flag signals she may be racing slightly out of her ideal role.|

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: Ronald Harris's runner has a couple of eye-catching placed efforts (2nd twice) in his recent history but also strings of poor finishes; his natural inclination to race from off the pace is squeezed by the five-runner field and firm ground, and with a T14 of 0/3 and 26 days since his last run, his chance in a shape dominated by an uncontested leader is materially discounted.|

races.paceDynamic: Rosieisme Darling is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no other genuine pace horses to challenge her, she will bowl along comfortably from the gates and dictate a controlled tempo over the 5½f at Bath on firm ground. The three true hold-up horses — Lavender Bloom, Geemann, and Rogue Rebellion — will be settled in behind, though Geemann and Rogue Rebellion are redistributed into midfield on the map because there is more hold-up intent in this field than can realistically find the rear in a five-runner race. Reality Queen is also a hold-up operator, meaning Rosieisme Darling essentially faces no credible early pressure and can establish a rhythm entirely on her own terms. A lone, uncontested front-runner on firm ground at a flat track like Bath is a significant tactical advantage, and this shape strongly favours prominent runners or horses versatile enough to track and pounce, while true deep closers face the classic risk of an uncontested lead that never fully comes back to them.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rosieisme Darling's early sectionals — if Luke Morris allows her to bowl along without cover she could build a lead that simply never gets reduced on firm Bath ground.
Geemann is flagged as prone to fading in the finish; if he is prominent early in a small field, watch for him to drop away sharply in the final furlong and take rivals wide or cause interference.

Reality Queen is 11 days since her last run for a yard firing at 3/23 in a 14-day window — watch for signs she may need the run or, conversely, arrives fresh and sharp enough to track the leader and challenge.

With four hold-up or midfield horses behind one front-runner in a five-runner race on firm ground, watch for a compressed, slowly-run scenario where the field never spreads and position at the 1f pole becomes the decisive factor.

Rogue Rebellion's jockey Kieran O'Neill should be monitored for whether he attempts to push forward early rather than accept a rear position — if he does, it would alter the pace dynamic even in this small field.

runners_data.name: Neptune Legend
runners_data.note: In the form of his life with two recent wins at Goodwood over 6f on good ground; David Egan retains the ride for Tony Carroll who is firing at 8/40 over 14 days, and this drop back to 5½f on firm at Bath looks well within range for a horse operating from a hold-up position but who has strong late speed.

runners_data.name: Ten Club
runners_data.note: Five-month absence (148 days) is the dominant concern here — last win was over 7f at Stalls and this 5½f on firm is a sharp drop in trip; Joe Leavy takes the ride for Adrian Wintle (1/5 T14) and the fitness question mark makes it very hard to trust despite a capable profile when fresh.

runners_data.name: Hidden Verse
runners_data.note: Placed in similar firm conditions (5/6f/FIR in recent history) and wears a hood; in reality a natural hold-up horse whose preferred rear-end role is unavailable in this shape given the volume of closers, so Jack Doughty will need to improvise from a position that doesn't suit — the style-fit discount is real.

runners_data.name: Fancy Dancer
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has struggled for wins (one place from 15 runs in similar going), and though Hayley Turner's yard (0/5 T14) is quiet, the deeper concern is that Fancy Dancer's natural inclination to race from well off the pace is compromised by the crowded hold-up section — Jack Gilligan will find it hard to carve out an ideal run.

runners_data.name: Southbank
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine pace-setter and confirmed front-runner; Chris Gordon sends him here 30 days after last run with a consistent placed record over 6f at Stalls — the step back to 5½f on firm Bath ground suits a horse who can be found one-paced late, but the uncontested lead is a significant asset.

runners_data.name: Sisters In The Sky
runners_data.note: Tyler Heard partners this seven-year-old for Grace Harris (1/14 T14) who also runs Symbol Of Hope; a natural hold-up horse placed in recent starts over 6f on good and firm, Sisters In The Sky has the positional flexibility to sit closer than her style tag suggests and the 18-day turnaround looks fine.

runners_data.name: Symbol Of Hope
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who wears a hood and is a stablemate of Sisters In The Sky under the same Grace Harris/Tyler Heard combination; ran a DNF (0) last time and form figures include a 12-length beating at Goodwood, so confidence in this runner's current level is limited even if the going is fine.

runners_data.name: She Went Whoosh
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and Scott Dixon's runner comes back in trip from recent 7f and 6f runs at Goodwood and Stalls with modest figures; the 10-day turnaround is quick and, like several rivals here, the natural hold-up role this horse prefers is congested — Kieran O'Neill will need luck from the midfield slot.

races.paceDynamic: Southbank is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5½f Bath handicap on firm ground, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the early lead, Luke Morris can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off. The eight-runner field is heavily populated with hold-up horses — Hidden Verse, Fancy Dancer, Sisters In The Sky, Symbol Of Hope, and She Went Whoosh are all natural hold-up types who have been redistributed toward midfield on the map simply because there is no room for them all to race from the rear. With Southbank uncontested and setting a fair but not suicidal pace on quick ground, the race shape is likely to favour those who can sit just off the pace and produce a sustained finish rather than a deep late challenge, since the firm Bath track rewards horses travelling smoothly into contention. Neptune Legend and Ten Club, both genuine hold-up types with the ability to quicken, will need the pace to be strong enough to reel in a controlled Southbank — that is the key tactical question. This shape most clearly favours a prominent or close-up tracking profile: a horse who can sit second or third, avoid traffic, and produce a clean run from two furlongs out on ground that tends to suit those traveling with cover rather than launching from deep.

watchPoints.text: Southbank (Luke Morris) — if allowed to steal a soft lead unchallenged from the off, the entire field is chasing a controlled front-runner on firm ground with every yard counting; watch whether any horse attempts to go with him in the first furlong.

Neptune Legend — arrives on a hat-trick bid with two recent wins and a top jockey; if David Egan can position him in second or third early rather than settling deep, the revised race shape significantly elevates his danger rating.

Ten Club — five months off and dropping sharply in trip to 5½f for the first time; watch the parade ring and early market moves for signs of stable confidence, as a well-backed returning runner would reframe the scenario probabilities.

Sisters In The Sky and Symbol Of Hope are saddled by the same trainer (Grace Harris) and both run from the same hold-up pool — watch which jockey (Tyler Heard vs Ashley Lewis 5lb claimer) settles better in the early stages, as stable tactics may favour one over the other.

Firm ground at Bath has been consistent across all three earlier 5½f races today — any track bias toward a particular draw or rail position should be noted from those results before this race goes off.

runners_data.name: Havana's Dream
runners_data.note: Modest OR-32 hold-up type whose recent form reads poorly — three starts at Goodwood and Sandown yielded nothing better than fifth — and although going is marked OK, this horse's profile offers little to suggest she reverses that trend; sits further forward on the map than her natural style but her chance looks slim regardless.

runners_data.name: Knightmare
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes over on this David Evans-trained four-year-old who has solid placed form including two seconds and a third in his last six, and firm going is an unknown but he handles a range of surfaces; his natural rear-of-field style means he's been brought forward on the map — he's a genuine closer who will need things to happen in front of him.

runners_data.name: Letsbeatsepsis
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's lightly-campaigned four-year-old arrives after 22 days off with recent form showing a pair of seconds at Goodwood over 1m2f; dropping back to a mile is worth noting and Rhys Clutterbuck takes the ride — a natural hold-up horse who may be able to actually secure a prominent position given her tactical versatility.

runners_data.name: Monks Mead
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, Tyler Heard aboard for Mark Usher who sent out one winner in 13 runners over 14 days; this five-year-old's recent form over 8-10f shows consistency if not brilliance, and on this uncontested firm-ground lead over a mile at Bath he is the key pace influence regardless of price.

runners_data.name: Baynoona
runners_data.note: Sue Gardner's five-year-old mare carries a visor and has one placed effort from two starts on firm, with Millie Wonnacott's 5lb claim a small asset; she is a natural closer pushed into the midfield map position — her going stats are thin but she's not without a shout if the race falls apart in front.

runners_data.name: Blue Hero
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle has been busy (2/13 in 14 days) and this veteran eight-year-old has back-to-back placed efforts on firm ground from a total of five such runs; Joe Leavy rides a horse who naturally settles deep in the field but has been mapped into midfield — he's a genuine hold-up performer who needs a strong pace.

runners_data.name: Eye Of The Water
runners_data.note: Ronald Harris's ten-year-old veteran handled a competitive card eight days ago and Luke Morris rides, though the trainer has only one runner in 14 days; a consistent if modest closer who has placed at Goodwood on good ground, he's a natural rear-of-field type pushed into midfield on this map and needs everything to go right.

runners_data.name: Hammal
runners_data.note: Max Young's five-year-old carries a finish-fade flag with a recent form string of 6/7000 — deeply uninspiring; Kieran O'Neill rides and the horse has been placed at Sandown and Kempton in sprint distances, suggesting this mile trip may be a stretch, and there is no compelling reason to expect improvement.

runners_data.name: Olivia Jane
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's four-year-old wears a hood and has a form line of 4000-6, with two entries at 16 furlongs in her history suggesting she's been campaigned over a range of trips; William Cox rides, and the recent form offers nothing — this is a hold-up type with limited evidence of a return to form.

runners_data.name: Scenario
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's prolific yard (7/62 in 14 days) saddles this four-year-old who won over a mile at Goodwood on good, showing he can handle a true mile; Silvestre De Sousa is a significant booking and this horse's one win in similar going conditions makes him the most interesting form angle in the hold-up group despite firm ground being a query.

runners_data.name: Star Of Atlantis
runners_data.note: Second Adrian Wintle runner alongside Blue Hero, ridden by David Egan who is a strong jockey booking; form of -98584 is disappointing and all five recent runs came at Sandown on standard, meaning the firm Bath ground is an unknown — a natural closer placed into midfield, he'd need significant improvement on known form.

runners_data.name: Addmann
runners_data.note: Joe Tickle's three-year-old gets a 9lb weight allowance off the older horses and carries a finish-fade flag alongside a form string of 7880-8 — poor recent form; Taylor Fisher rides, and while all runs have come over shorter trips than today's mile, the horse is mapped forward of his natural hold-up position and showed nothing at Goodwood last time.

runners_data.name: Due Destiny
runners_data.note: Patrick Owens has no runners in the 14-day record and this three-year-old wears a hood, arriving 23 days fresh; form of 704-55 over sprint trips up to 7f raises questions about seeing out a mile, and as a natural hold-up type mapped into midfield, Harry Vigors's 5lb claim is the only tangible plus here.

races.paceDynamic: Monks Mead is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field on firm ground at Bath, and with no genuine rival likely to match that early pace, he will be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo without being pressured or forced into a pace war. That creates a smooth, metronomic gallop over the mile — the kind of surface-skimming firm-ground lead that can be notoriously difficult to reel in at Bath, where the track's natural camber and tight turns reward those who get first run. The field is overwhelmingly hold-up in profile, meaning the majority of runners will be forced to track the pace rather than lead or challenge prominently, compressing the midfield and making it harder for genuine closers to find gaps or generate momentum. Tactically, this race shape strongly favours horses who can sit close to a single, uncontested pace-setter and respond early — prominent-to-mid-division types who can turn the final bend in a good position benefit most. The field holds far more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Knightmare, Blue Hero, Star Of Atlantis, Baynoona, Eye Of The Water, and others are all redistributed into midfield, with Monks Mead and perhaps Letsbeatsepsis best placed to actually secure their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Monks Mead is the lone front-runner and his ability to control this race from the front unchallenged is the single most important tactical factor — if he jumps well and establishes an early lead, he sets the shape for every other runner.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types including Knightmare, Blue Hero, Star Of Atlantis and Baynoona will all be competing for the same midfield real estate; watch for traffic problems and crowding on the home turn as they look for gaps simultaneously.

Scenario's booking of Silvestre De Sousa for the Tony Carroll yard — which has seven winners from 62 in 14 days — is an eye-catching combination; De Sousa is likely to position this horse more prominently than his natural style suggests, which could be decisive.

Firm ground is confirmed throughout the card and has been consistent all day — horses with proven form on firm (Knightmare, Blue Hero, Baynoona) hold a meaningful surface edge over the large portion of this field who are unproven or have concerns on fast going.

Three-year-olds Addmann and Due Destiny receive a 9lb weight allowance from older rivals but both have uninspiring form over shorter trips — watch whether they can get competitive over a mile, or whether the drop in class is insufficient to offset the trip concern.

runners_data.name: Sant Alessio
runners_data.note: Won twice from hold-up at Sandown over this trip in similar conditions and has strong course form, making this a live chance at OR 69 for an in-form yard; Taylor Fisher is a capable claimer and the horse's ability to travel prominently enough to avoid being caught behind slow-moving hold-up rivals is the key tactical question.

runners_data.name: Thiscouldbefun
runners_data.note: Shaped well when fourth at Sandown and has a win on this trip at Yarmouth, but its natural rear-of-field style has been squeezed into a midfield berth by the cluster of hold-up horses in this race, meaning it is unlikely to get the clean daylight it needs to fire; the hold-up discount (0.93 STYLE_FIT) is a genuine concern here.

runners_data.name: Post Rider
runners_data.note: The race's sole confirmed front runner, OR 75 top-weight, trained by Oliver Cole whose yard has hit form (2 from 15 in 14 days), and with a course win on record — controlling this race from the front on firm ground is a very realistic outcome and the absence of any pace rival is a significant tactical asset.

runners_data.name: Nakaaha
runners_data.note: Ran second on firm ground in his last start over this course and distance, giving him the most directly relevant form in the race; he races prominently under David Egan and is ideally placed to stalk Post Rider and challenge turning for home, though five consecutive defeats since that second tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Swiped
runners_data.note: Won last time out over a mile at Goodwood (good ground) and is Ralph Beckett's yard representative at OR 72, suggesting he retains ability; he is a natural hold-up horse but this low-pressure pace may not generate the gap he needs, and racing on good ground throughout his career makes firm Bath his first real going test.

runners_data.name: Naval Ensign
runners_data.note: Won on straight-track Yarmouth over seven furlongs on standard and has shown ability, but is a genuine hold-up horse (headgear: hood/tongue) operating at OR 59 whose true style has been mapped into midfield by this crowded rear — the style penalty (0.92) is material and an apprentice booking further lowers expectations.

runners_data.name: Ebn Sabt
runners_data.note: Young three-year-old for Ben Lund (0 from 2 in 14 days) with modest recent form — a run of 1-4-6-7-7 in the last five outings tells a declining story; a true hold-up type now competing out of position in midfield with a 0.91 STYLE_FIT score and the least experienced jockey in the field, making this a difficult assignment.

races.paceDynamic: Post Rider is the sole confirmed front runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing to press from the outset, is set to dictate a controlled, measured pace on firm ground over one mile at Bath. That uncontested lead means the fractions are unlikely to be truly searching, creating a rail-hugging, compressed race where those tracking in second and third will have first use of any acceleration. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the controlled tempo and pounce before hold-up horses can wind up from off the pace — Nakaaha and Sant Alessio fit the positional sweet spot, with Swiped the classic closer who needs the pace to be honest enough to close. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear: Thiscouldbefun, Ebn Sabt, and Naval Ensign are all true come-from-behind horses who will be shuffled into a midfield berth rather than their natural position, meaning their finishing kicks are likely to be blunted by the lack of genuine early pace.

watchPoints.text: Post Rider's uncontested lead is the race's dominant tactical fact — if Lewis Edmunds finds an untroubled rail position and controls the fractions, the runner-up spot may be the best closers can manage.
Nakaaha's quick turnaround (8 days since last run) is worth monitoring in the paddock — if he shows signs of wear, his usually prominent jumping style could be compromised rounding the home bend.

Swiped steps onto firm ground for the first time having run exclusively on good at Goodwood; if the going inconveniences him, his finishing kick may arrive a furlong too late on this unique Bath track.

Three redistributed hold-up horses (Thiscouldbefun, Naval Ensign, Ebn Sabt) all carry style-fit discounts of 0.91–0.93 and are likely to be racing out of their natural position — watch to see which can find a clear run in the straight despite less-than-ideal positioning early.

Bath's unique uphill-then-downhill one-mile track tends to compress the field turning in, which can cause bunching for hold-up horses; runners caught wide or pocketed at the three-furlong pole rarely recover on this surface.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Days
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Ashley Lewis (claiming 5lb) and Syd Hosie, whose modest 0/2 T14 figures are a minor caution; form figures of 985-70 show inconsistency but the Firm going is not a concern and 11 days since last run is a fresh enough gap for a horse who handles similar conditions.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Charm
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner here and the race's pivotal tactical factor; William Cox takes the ride for Georgina Nicholls, whose 0/3 T14 record tempers confidence, and the headgear (blinkers) suggests she needs holding together — but uncontested on Firm ground over a long flat Bath trip she sets the agenda for everyone else.

runners_data.name: Offiah's Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who is the only horse likely to push Sea Of Charm early, though his recent string of 0s and poor finishes at Goodwood and Southwell on varying ground make it hard to be enthusiastic; Joe Tickle's yard has a live 1/15 T14 strike rate and the step back up to 1m3½f (where his best effort was a second on similar ground) is his main hope.

runners_data.name: Lakota Chief
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has run only three times, all over 7-8f at Sandown — this 1m3½f trip is a significant step into unknown territory; Pierre-Louis Jamin is a sharp jockey to have aboard an Archie Watson-trained improver (yard 1/14 T14), and his true style is hold-up, placed into midfield here only because the rear of the field is overpopulated with closers.

runners_data.name: We Ride At Dawn
runners_data.note: Hold-up three-year-old whose best run was a second over 1m2f at Goodwood on Good ground, showing a genuine staying profile; Robert Edwards has a modest 0/2 T14 record and 30 days between runs is routine, but on Firm ground over this trip his stamina credentials make him one of the more convincing threats from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Barak Warrior
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa takes the mount on this three-year-old who has finished 7-8th in all three starts, all on Good or Soft at Goodwood — Firm ground is an open question and the trip extension is significant; his natural style is genuine hold-up but he is operating from a mapped midfield position because the true back of the field is crowded, adding a positional complication to an already uncertain profile.

runners_data.name: Campeona
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's two-year-old filly returning after 186 days off — the Prescott yard is renowned for having horses spot-on after a break, and a T14 rate of 2/8 supports that angle; all three starts have been over 7-8f at Sandown on Standard or similar, so both the Firm ground and this 1m3½f trip are untested, and her hold-up style leaves her dependent on a truly run race that this shape may not deliver.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Of Charm is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press her from the off over this 1m3½f trip on fast ground at Bath, she is set to control proceedings at a pace entirely of her choosing. The seven-runner field is dominated by hold-up types — We Ride At Dawn, Pivotal Days, Lakota Chief, Barak Warrior, and Campeona are all natural closers, while Offiah's Boy is the only other prominent racer, though his recent form gives little cause to expect him to aggressively challenge for the lead. The field holds more hold-up horses than the pace map can place at the rear: Lakota Chief, Barak Warrior, and Campeona are genuine come-from-behind types who have been redistributed into midfield slots because the rear is congested, meaning their true tactical position may be even further back than shown. With Sea Of Charm able to bowl along in front unchallenged on Firm ground that suits galloping types, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finish, provided they can find daylight through a potentially bunched midfield group.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Charm holds a commanding position at the head of affairs with no one to challenge her — if she gets away cleanly and settles, she could prove very difficult to catch on Firm ground at Bath's flat track.

Lakota Chief, Barak Warrior, and Campeona are all genuine hold-up types crammed into a small rear group — watch for traffic problems in the straight if they all simultaneously seek a run, which could cost any one of them a placing.

Campeona's 186-day absence is a layoff to note — despite Prescott's excellent record returning horses, her Firm-ground and trip questions mean she is a watch-and-learn runner before committing to her in similar races.

Offiah's Boy is the only horse likely to apply even modest early pressure to Sea Of Charm; if he fails to go with her from the outset (as his poor recent form suggests is possible), Sea Of Charm's task becomes significantly easier and the closing fractions will tighten for the hold-up pack.

The entire card has returned Firm throughout the evening — ground is consistent and unlikely to ease, which removes one variable but means any horse with a Soft or Heavy preference is firmly disadvantaged by post time.
